chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Hilal from Yasir al-Khadam who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'I saw in a dream as if there was a cage containing seventeen bottles. The cage fell and the bottles broke.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If your dream is true, a man from my Household will emerge, rule for seventeen days, then die.' So Muhammad ibn Ibrahim emerged in Al-Kufa with Abu Al-Saraaya, and he remained for seventeen days, then died.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the contented one), a title of the 8th Shia Imam
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Al-Kufa, a major city in Iraq
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, a prominent figure in the Saffarid uprising

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the dream of seventeen bottles in the hadith of Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Rida (as) interprets a dream of seventeen broken bottles as a prophecy regarding the brief rule of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Saffar in Kufa, a key figure in the early Abbasid era. The interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of linking symbolic dreams to specific historical events within the Ahl al-Bayt's lineage, emphasizing the transient nature of their political authority during this period.

en.sarwar: 371. Al-Husayn Bin Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Yaser Al-Khadam who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Ridha (a.s.), ‘I saw (a dream) during the sleep, as if there was a cage in which were seventeen bottles. There was an impact upon the cage and the bottles broke’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘If your dream is true, a man from my (a.s.) Household would come out, govern for seventeen days, then die’. So Muhammad Bin Ibrahim came out at Al-Kufa along with Abu Al-Saraaya. So he remained for seventeen days, then died’.
